abstract: In this work, we revisit the generalized emergent dark energy model by confronting it with DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, in combination with joint CMB data from ACT, SPT, and Planck, as well as Type Ia supernova samples including Pantheon<math altimg="si1.svg"><msup><mrow/><mo>+</mo></msup></math>, DES-Dovekie, and Union3. We find that the GEDE model remains compatible with the ΛCDM paradigm, with no statistically significant preference for deviations when all datasets are combined. In particular, the key model parameter Δ is consistent with the ΛCDM value <math altimg="si22.svg"><mrow><mstyle mathvariant="normal"><mi>Δ</mi></mstyle><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> within 2σ once SNe Ia data are included. Despite this overall agreement, the GEDE model does not exhibit the phantom crossing suggested by DESI DR2. Instead, the evolution of the dark energy equation of state w(z) indicates that the model behaves either as a full phantom (<math altimg="si23.svg"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak"><</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>) or quintessence (<math altimg="si24.svg"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">></mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>), depending on the dataset combination, without a clear transition across <math altimg="si25.svg"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. When Pantheon<math altimg="si1.svg"><msup><mrow/><mo>+</mo></msup></math> data are included, the model converges closely to ΛCDM with <math altimg="si26.svg"><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≃</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. The GEDE model does not alleviate the existing cosmological tensions. The inferred values of H0 remain in the range <math altimg="si27.svg"><mrow><mn>67.9</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mn>69.8</mn><mspace width="0.33em"/><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">km</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mtext>Mpc</mtext><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></math>, while the sound horizon rd and clustering parameter S8 remain consistent with ΛCDM, failing to resolve the H0 and S8 tensions. Finally, both Gaussian significance levels ( < 2σ) and Bayesian evidence (ln Bi,j < 1) indicate no statistically significant preference for GEDE over ΛCDM. We conclude that, although DESI DR2 hints at dynamical dark energy, the GEDE model remains observationally indistinguishable from ΛCDM and does not support the Quintom-B-type behavior suggested by DESI DR2.
title: No preference for generalized emergent dark energy from current cosmological data
